title: The Sooner Schooner Penalty: What Happened at the 1985 Orange Bowl
question: Did the Sooner Schooner really cause a penalty in the 1985 Orange Bowl?
answer: Yes. In the January 1, 1985 Orange Bowl against Washington, the Schooner rolled out to celebrate a field goal that had been wiped out by a penalty, drawing a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct flag. The longer kick was blocked and OU lost 28-17.
summary: In the Jan. 1, 1985 Orange Bowl, the Sooner Schooner celebrated a nullified field goal, drew a 15-yard flag, and OU lost 28-17 to Washington. The full story.
body: The Sooner Schooner has celebrated thousands of points, but one of its most famous rides came after points that did not count. It happened in the Orange Bowl in Miami on January 1, 1985, with No. 2 Oklahoma facing No. 4 Washington and the score tied 14-14.

Tim Lashar knocked through a 22-yard field goal, and the Schooner crew did what it always does, heading onto the field to celebrate. The problem was that the kick had already been nullified by an illegal procedure penalty, reportedly because a player had not reported a temporary jersey number. On a soggy field, the wagon bogged down near the Washington sideline, and officials added a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

Those two flags pushed the attempt back 20 yards. Lashar's 42-yard try was blocked, and the game stayed tied. Washington took control from there and won 28-17, with tailback Jacque Robinson and defensive tackle Ron Holmes earning MVP honors. Barry Switzer later made clear he did not consider the wagon the deciding factor.

The game mattered beyond the bowl itself. Orange Bowl organizers had envisioned it as a national championship game, but undefeated BYU claimed the title after beating Michigan in the Holiday Bowl. Washington finished second in both final polls, and Oklahoma slipped to sixth. Today the Schooner still travels to bowl games, but because of turf concerns it no longer runs on the field anywhere except at home.
